findings.claim: The original editor chooses the first non-sentinel height in X-major scan order for the entire grading rectangle and otherwise falls back to the plane-0 anchor, allowing transitive height propagation across overlapping objects.
findings.limitations: Exact original x87 corner rounding and individual retail mission causality are not reproduced.

findings.claim: Material 6 or 7 assignment by object classes 0x50-0x53 is independent of the height-origin priority, so overlap may retain one object's height and another's material.
findings.limitations: No original editable workspace insertion order is available for shipped missions.

findings.claim: Grading traverses numeric zone buckets in order and each object list head-first, while new/moved/loaded objects are head-inserted, making later processing and material precedence distinct from global creation order.
findings.limitations: Any other list mutation or saved workspace order changes the sequence.

findings.claim: Native grading first loads object +0x0C height from plane 0 at the anchor, then stamps an asymmetric integer AABB range derived from rotated corners, with zero-minimum adjustment.
findings.limitations: No live editor workspace test of cell boundaries; coordinates are grid-cell indices.

findings.claim: The native post-grade condition compares zero-extended AX against 0xffffffff and cannot be true; on this path object +0x0C is updated even when sampled uint16 height equals 0x8000.

The editor commits a fully buffered zone's smoothing result to plane 1 before processing the next zone in the same pass, permitting later-zone border samples to see already updated neighbor-zone heights.
findings.limitations: Analytical illustration is not original-code execution; numeric magnitude of cross-zone differences unmeasured.

findings.claim: Historical v20 intersection data have material 6/7 in 381 of 386 placement footprints but 15 of 19 largest worst-point discrepancies occur on material 0 or 1; presence of 6/7 cannot by itself explain anomalies.

evidence.ref: private v20 archived footprint diagnostic TSVs

findings.limitations: Static original retail samples, not causal reconstruction of editor authoring history.
